sections.value:
**Performance: BLOCK** at `0a693ca73abf7a81cb3cd3f6f63d70978ddd3e83`, for one normal-use restart failure, **P219-F001**.

**The Rust CLI retries with the old boot credential.** `DaemonClient::new` reads the current key once into `self.token` (`client.rs:164-169`). `transmit` applies `self.auth(request)` once outside its retry loop and clones that already-authenticated request (`client.rs:564-592`). Every successful daemon boot generates a fresh key (`daemon/auth.rs:120-143`) and publishes it after binding, before serving (`daemon/lib.rs:919-930,1121-1132`).

A normal `pij-rs directory`/`requests` call can capture the previous key just before the port closes, get connection refusals, then connect to the restarted daemon **still carrying the previous key**. It receives an authentication refusal rather than recovering the command. No credential refresh exists in this Rust retry path. This is the normal bounce race F174 intends to fix, not an optional hardening case.

The current recovery test uses a fixed synthetic key and a fake server that does not validate rotated authentication, so green CI establishes TCP reconnection, not recovery across a real boot-key rotation. Correct this credential lifecycle without replaying a write that reached a handler, and prove that specific reconnect case in CI. No real key was read by this review; the finding is from source.

**Requested cost checks otherwise pass:** reachable requests keep one network attempt and no added process; new clock/clone/whitelist bookkeeping is in-process. Default pauses250ms,500ms,1s,2s,4s,4s,4s,4s total19.75s: at most nine attempts per restart phase, scaling with concurrent active requests, not seats per tick. Larger explicit CLI/router overrides permit more attempts. JS budgets count sleep time rather than a hard end-to-end20s wall deadline; existing caller cancellation/deadlines still matter. Existing auth-refresh phases can add another request/phase, so nine is not an unconditional whole-tool-call bound.

Rust's listed ping/hook/activity/FYI-claim/register/whoami/trailer/spawn-child paths retain zero restart wait. OMP opts in only send/spawn; Copilot only send. Registration, inbox, stream and turn-boundary routes do not acquire this new inner retry. The router retries only its absent/refused health probe before dispatch. HTTP replies, resets and timeouts do not enter the new transport-refusal loop. `PIJ_RS_RESTART_WAIT_MS` applies to the Rust CLI/router, as documented; extension tools use their configured/default budget.

**Exact-head proof:** [CI 42764036542](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42764036542), Rust job `129656199508`, successful-upload artifact **13739600549**, matching trigger-head metadata: **2,416 executed passed**, zero failures/errors; six skips separately reported by nextest. JUnit names reconnect, exhausted wait, accepted-request-sent-once and env-override cases. Node22 npm2,287 passed/six skipped; native350 passed/zero skipped, including restart behavior. Node24, Rust lint and delivers succeed; worktree clean and matching GitHub head/CLEAN. These results do not cover P219-F001.

No local product build/test, daemon bounce, synthetic requests or credential-file read. The separate authorized baseline/profile does not exercise this branch.
